served.stem: Which cells of the stomach lining secrete hydrochloric acid?
served.bankWhy: Sort the stomach lining by what each cell hands over. Parietal cells pump out hydrochloric acid and also make intrinsic factor for vitamin B12 absorption, while chief cells release pepsinogen, the inactive form of the protein digesting enzyme. The acid from the parietal cells is what converts pepsinogen into active pepsin, so pair them as parietal for acid and chief for enzyme.

answer.line: Parietal cells pump H+ into the stomach with their H+/K+ ATPase, and Cl- follows. They also make intrinsic factor.

steps: Sort the cells by their products.
Parietal cells make the acid with a proton pump, plus intrinsic factor for vitamin B12.
Chief cells make pepsinogen, which the acid switches on. Mucous cells make mucus, and G cells make gastrin.

choices.note: Chief cells sit right beside parietal cells, which is why they pull. They release pepsinogen, the enzyme precursor the acid then activates.
Goblet cells make mucus in the intestine and airways. The stomach's mucus comes from its own surface and neck cells.
The proton pump of the parietal cell; Cl- follows the H+.
They make the mucus that protects the lining from the acid, not the acid itself.
G cells release gastrin, the hormone that tells parietal cells to make acid. Pick them and you stop one step before the source.
